title: Make Your First Masjid Visit
whyMatters: A masjid can give you prayer support, community, classes, and a place to ask real people for help. Your first visit does not need to be perfect; it just needs to be gentle and manageable.

subSteps: A smaller daily prayer can feel easier than a crowded Friday prayer.
Check the masjid website or call ahead if you are unsure.
Ask whether they have new Muslim support or visitor help.
Wear clean, loose clothing that covers your body comfortably.
Women can bring a scarf if they plan to enter the prayer area.
Do not panic if you are not dressed like everyone else.
Remove your shoes where others remove theirs.
If you are unsure where to go, ask someone near the entrance.
You can simply say you are a new Muslim and this is your first visit.
Ask who handles convert support or beginner classes.
Leave if you feel overwhelmed; you can return another day.

obstacles.problem: I am afraid people will stare
obstacles.solution: Most people are focused on prayer. If someone notices you are new, many will be happy to help. You can also call ahead and ask someone to meet you.

obstacles.problem: I do not know which entrance to use
obstacles.solution: Look for signs, follow the flow of people, or ask at the door. Some masjids have separate prayer areas; asking is normal.

tinyVersion: Call or message one masjid and ask when a beginner can visit.
unlocksNext: Your first visit makes Jumuah, classes, and mentorship easier to approach.

commonQuestions.problem: Can I visit if I cannot pray properly yet?
commonQuestions.solution: Yes. You can observe, follow what you can, and ask for help. A masjid should be a place to learn, not only a place for people who already know everything.

gentleScripts.title: At the entrance
gentleScripts.body: Assalamu alaykum. I am a new Muslim and this is my first time here. Could you show me where to go?
